title: json: fix buffer overflow in string_unescape()
description:
Fixes a potential buffer overflow issue in string_unescape() with a redesign
to be more robust against invalid input.

It makes use of wmem_strbuf API now.

Closes #17475

I saw that some tests did fail.
![json](/uploads/78f6b3bfb947e5ea00952e1dd415a233/json.png)

I think the reason is an unintended sligh change in the behaviour because string values are exported with quotation marks which not not have been the case in previous versions.

Which way to go? 

**A)** Adjust the test scripts 

or 

**B)** ensure value string are being exported without quotation marks?

I think the additional quotation marks might be helpful when string contain whitespaces for example.

This fixes the the crashes for each of the capture files in #17475 for me here. Tested with

```
WIRESHARK_DEBUG_WMEM_OVERRIDE=simple G_SLICE=always-malloc lldb --batch -o 'pr lau -- -nVr /path/to/clusterfuzz-testcase-xxxx.pcap' ./run/tshark
```

That's good to hear. How to proceed with the other tests which appear to fail?


I vote for omitting the quotation marks in the dissection output. Plenty of other protocols have fields that might include spaces, and as far as I know we don't quote them.
I have removed the additional quotation marks.
